topic: Stub Libraries in Shared Library Linking
explanation: Stub libraries are intermediary files created during the linking process of shared libraries (like DLLs on Windows or .so files on Linux).  They act as placeholders, providing symbol definitions for the actual shared library without containing the library's code or data. This allows the linker to resolve symbols during the linking of the application, even before the shared library is loaded at runtime.  This is crucial for dynamic linking, enabling applications to use shared libraries without needing to be relinked every time the library is updated.
code_example:
# 1. Shared Library Creation (Implementation)
# Defines the actual code/data
gcc -c -fPIC feature.c -o feature.o
gcc -shared feature.o -o libfeature.so

# 2. Stub/Import Library Generation (Definition Placeholder)
# Stub provides symbol references (definitions), NOT code
# Linux example (extract symbols into a minimal archive):
objcopy --extract-symbol libfeature.so libfeature.a

# Windows example (generates import library .lib):
# Requires a definition file (feature.def)
lib /def:feature.def /out:libfeature.lib

# 3. Application Linking Phase
# Application links against the stub library (.a or .lib)
# Stub resolves symbols during link-time
gcc main.o -L. -lfeature -o my_application

# Dynamic Loader (Runtime)
# Dynamic loader finds and loads libfeature.so when my_application starts
# (Linker used stub; OS loader uses actual shared library)
keywords: Import library, Dynamic linking, Symbol resolution, Stub library
